fields.summary: Need to clarify meaning of root cardinality
fields.customfield_10618:
In the table here: [http://build.fhir.org/elementdefinition.html#interpretation]         

         will drop the "(irrelevant)" comment from first repetition min/max and instead add another dagger pointing to a new bullet below the table that says:

         The cardinality on a type places constraints on references to that type.  I.e. profiles referencing the type must fall within the cardinality bounds of the type itself.  This most commonly occurs with Extension profiles, where the profile may prohibit the extension from repeating (max=1), or less commonly, make the extension mandatory (min=1) - i.e. if the extension is referenced in a profile, it must be marked as mandatory.
fields.description:
[https://chat.fhir.org/#narrow/stream/4-implementers/subject/cardinality.20of.20root.20elements]         

         We currently say that the root cardinality is meaningless, but it's actually not - it constrains the cardinality permitted for references to the type - and that types claiming to comply with the type are bound to.  We should make that explicit.

comments.body: We discussed this at length during a WGM...Atlanta I think, and came to the point of view reflected in the current spec, that is, cardinality on the root element is irrelevant and the snapshot generator (and validator) should not pull the root element's cardinality into the snapshot element for a referencing element.

Extension definitions must be able to constrain the cardinality of the appearance of the extension in the profiles that reference them.  That's always been the case and is still needed.  It's not a question of pulling the root element cardinality into the snapshot, it's ensuring that the snapshot complies with the cardinality in the definition.

resolution.description: The proposed change will be made as suggested
